predict.help: align reads with a trained model -> AIRR TSV

options.help: a model file (.alignair), a registry id or id@version, or hf://org/repo
a registry url to look model ids up in (repeatable)
never touch the network
pin a Hugging Face branch/tag/commit (for hf://org/repo) or a catalog version
Hugging Face token for a private/gated repo (falls back to $HF_TOKEN, then $HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN)
reads to align (FASTA / FASTQ / TSV; .gz ok; '-' = stdin)
output AIRR TSV path
sequence column name (CSV/TSV input)
id column name (CSV/TSV input)
write dropped/invalid input records here (id, position, reason, sequence)

locus label for records the model can't attribute (default: the model's locus if it declares exactly one; else IGH). With several loci, each record carries its called V's locus (blank without a V call).
do not write the <out>.run.json sidecar
output columns: a preset (full/core/minimal/airr) or a comma-separated field list (default: full). Light selections skip the AIRR assembly for speed.
per-read metadata table (e.g. 10x filtered_contig_annotations.csv / an AIRR TSV) to join by id and carry into output (cell_id/barcode/umi_count/…)
id column in the --metadata table
comma-separated metadata columns to carry through (default: known 10x/AIRR set)

a donor's genotype: JSON/YAML {V|D|J: [allele names]} (calls come only from the alleles of each segment it names) or the AIRR GenotypeSet `alignair genotype` writes (genes it does not name keep all their alleles); a subset of the reference (--reference may add novel alleles)

germline FASTA (V, D and J alleles) to call from, novel alleles included. A missing IMGT gap or anchor is taken from the same allele in the model's own reference, for a V also from a close same-length variant, else found from the sequence

infer the donor's V genotype from the reads' own calls (TIgGER's frequency rule on the reads whose V call is a single allele) and re-call the reads whose call it excludes while they tie an allele it allows; writes the genotype to --genotype-out. Reads the input twice
where --infer-genotype writes the genotype, an AIRR GenotypeSet (default: <out>.genotype.json)
--infer-genotype: the share of a gene's single-allele reads its alleles explain (default 0.875)
--infer-genotype: the single-allele reads a gene needs to be genotyped; a gene with fewer keeps every allele (default 10)
cpu / cuda / mps / auto (default: auto: CUDA, then Apple MPS, then CPU)
reads per batch (default: 256 on a GPU, 16 per worker with --threads on the CPU, else 64)
CPU threads: on the CPU, N worker processes of one thread each (torch's threads scale poorly on read batches); on a GPU, torch's CPU threads (default: one process on torch's own thread count)
stream the input in chunks of this many reads (default 20000)
fail the job if the AIRR-assembly FAILURE rate exceeds this fraction (default 0.01); failures are always tagged per row regardless
fail the job if the PARTIAL-assembly rate exceeds this fraction (default 1.0 = never; partial rows are always tagged with a reason)
never fail on assembly failure/partial rates (dirty repertoires); still tags rows
suppress the update-available notice
include the full exception traceback on errors
runtime error format on stderr (default: text)
